version.value: Unaccompanied motet for cantus, altus, tenor, second tenor and bassus
version.note: The five-part score is the motet, not the Mass of the same name. The album lists the motet as track 1 and the Mass movements separately. The choir’s exact performing edition and pitch are not identified.

publication.note: 1569 is publication, not an asserted exact composition year. Suggestions that it may be an early work are not converted into a date.

text.value: Song of Songs, beginning with the lily among thorns comparison, followed by Alleluia
text.note: The text is described as a whole; no line is assigned an exact timestamp without alignment.

completeness.note: No Mass movement is appended, and no editorial audio excerpt is made.

scoreEdition.value: Theodor de Witt, Palestrina’s Werke, volume I, Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1862, plate 10414
scoreEdition.note: Public-domain edition. Motet No. 21 spans printed pp. 90–94, PDF pp. 104–108; those pages were opened and viewed, including the final cadence on p. 94.

performers.note: These are credits for the nominated recording, not the separate Hyperion performances consulted for programme notes. Individual singers and choir size are not identified.

date.note: FMA describes a live minidisc recording and gives the album date as 29 July 2007. The choir’s own archive documents the matching Renaissance Influences programme on that date. Their conjunction supports a probable session date, but the track description does not explicitly identify the session day. The FMA track’s 20 August 2010 is its online release.

place.value: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Hill Street, Wellington, New Zealand
place.note: The official archive supplies the venue for the matching 29 July 2007 concert. The link between that concert and the recording is inferred from title, director, programme and album date, not stated in the track description.

label.note: No original recording label or commercial imprint is named; Free Music Archive is the distribution platform.

catalogue.note: The album title and track number are known, but no release catalogue number is supplied.

matrixTakeSides.note: The source describes a live minidisc recording, not a pressed disc matrix; no session take number is supplied.

album.value: Renaissance influences — Pizzetti: Messa di Requiem / Palestrina: Missa Sicut lilium inter spinas, track 1
album.note: The motet remains an independently authored recording here; the album is not turned into a multi-movement set.

credits.value: Commons import from FMA by ComputerHotline
credits.note: The recording or minidisc-transfer engineer is not named. The uploader credit does not imply that ComputerHotline made the original recording.

date.note: The online track release is 20 August 2010; the Commons upload is 11 April 2020. No separate minidisc transfer or mastering date is established.

processing.value: Live minidisc source; FMA MP3 converted to Ogg for Commons, with Wikimedia MP3 access derivative
processing.note: The source format chain is described by the album and Commons source entry. Microphone placement, equalisation, noise reduction and any earlier editing are unknown. No additional trim by Contrapunctus.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative of the Commons Ogg import from FMA

composition.note: The 1569 work and public-domain 1862 score are distinct from the Tudor Consort’s modern performance rights.

recording.note: The external FMA track was opened directly and explicitly licenses the Tudor Consort performance under CC BY 3.0; no NonCommercial restriction is attached. Commons still displays a pending external licence review, so that template is not treated as a passed review. Independent FMA evidence supports the actual sound recording licence.
